target_customer: Developers and EPC contractors building utility-scale solar farms and data centers, plus NASA for lunar construction
problem: Large infrastructure builds are constrained by scarce labor. Cosmic-1 is a 10,000 lb autonomous robot for heavy-lift manipulation such as placing solar panels, working with human crews.
business_model: Robotic equipment and services sold to construction customers via quote; also a NASA contract per the YC page

founders.name: James Emerick
education: University of Pennsylvania, BS and MS mechanical engineering

founders.name: Lewis Jones
education: Caltech, BS mechanical engineering and economics
founders.background_notes: Named to Forbes 30 Under 30 per the YC page.

competitors.name: AES Maximo
competitors.what: In-house solar installation robot by developer AES
competitors.traction_then: expanding fleet toward a 100 MW installation target for 2025

competitors.name: Luminous Robotics
competitors.what: LUMI solar installation robot designed to fit existing workflows

technical_complexity.rationale: Heavy autonomous manipulation outdoors with custom hardware, perception and safety around crews is research grade for an eight person team.

defensibility.rationale: Hardware plus field deployment data is harder to copy than software, but several funded rivals and utility developers build similar machines.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Rivals kept building; later entrants Gritt and Planted announced large rounds in 2026. No acquisition of Cosmic found.

market_need_then: Utility-scale solar for data centers needs fast installation with limited labor. Cosmic reports more than doubled crew productivity and a DOE American-Made Solar Prize award per Robotics 24/7.

identity.voice_and_tone: Short, direct and mission focused with the stated goal of building a city on Mars.

branding.brand_signature: The goal of building a city on Mars with autonomous robots
branding.community_and_virality: Won the Built Worlds Construction Tech 2026 Demo Day and drew press on its Mars goal; a separate company called Cosmic Buildings causes name overlap.

brand_strength.rationale: The Mars mission gives a memorable story that press repeats, but the name is generic and nothing shows brand driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Cosmic Robotics raised 4 million dollars led by Giant Ventures in April 2025, deployed Cosmic-1 on large US solar farms and joined YC Summer 2026, expanding into data centers with a NASA lunar contract. Founders come from Built Robotics and Relativity Space. Well funded solar robotics rivals appeared in 2026. Outcome is still open.
notes: Robotics 24/7 does not state the stage; TechCrunch reportedly calls it pre-seed while other outlets say seed, so the stage is recorded as other. A JLL Foundation grant and a 350 thousand dollar SAFE appear only in single sources and are not recorded as rounds. Founding year given as 2024 by YC and 2023 by one outlet. Competitor list is as of the April 2025 round; Gritt and Planted emerged later. NASA contract comes from the YC page only.
